values: Target span under FLOATING SOLIDS OR VISIBLE FOAM (Page 5, Section part_i)

Adjacent structural context showing this Part I section is a narrative effluent condition without an accompanying numeric limit value or parameter-specific sampling-frequency table in the immediately surrounding pages
rationale: The packet provides the target clause and adjacent Part I pages but does not establish, to the burden required for ACCEPT or REJECT, whether the enumerated effects condition the floating-materials discharge prohibition or constitute separate, independently applicable prohibitions. The Page 5 excerpt uses a single integrated 'no discharge of oils, scum, grease and other floating materials that would cause ... or would damage ...' construction; surface syntax is consistent with a conditioning relative clause, but the packet contains no regulatory interpretation authority, enforcement guidance, or structural parse that would establish how this provision is meant to operate as law. Adjacent pages confirm the section is a narrative effluent condition without a numeric limit or parameter-specific sampling-frequency table (page 4 shows a WET monitoring table; page 5 is narrative only; page 6 begins Part II), yet that structural fact does not resolve the conditioning-versus-separate-prohibition fork. The packet itself records that it may be evidence-insufficient. Neither the conditioning reading nor the separate-prohibitions reading is grounded strongly enough to close the obligation, so UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
